note: Application keys (SPEC 3.9): top-level keys whose names contain U+002E FULL STOP, whose values are any JSON value, carried verbatim and never reported. The file holds an array, an object, a string, a number and a null, and an empty array and an empty object beside them. The null and the two empty values are load-bearing: the absent-equals-empty rule of sections 3.1 and 8.1 does not apply to an application key, so the round trip catches a reader or writer that drops a key because its value is null or empty. Reverse-DNS form is guidance a reader must not validate, so `points.` and `.` are application keys; the value under `points.` would be an unusable top-level point, and no rule of the format applies inside it. The `style` object inside app.viatrail.rulesets, with its `importance` of 99, is application data, not a key of the format: it must survive untouched for the same reason. Dotted keys also sit inside the two opaque objects of section 3.10 (a data record body, and an application key's value, nested two deep in com.example.nested), where they are carried and not reported: the top-level-only rule of section 3.9 does not reach inside an opaque object. Application keys have no entry in counts, so the tree comparison is the only check on them.
